practices.practice: Keep the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string and credentials out of source control: read the connection string from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
practices.prior_belief: Read the DocumentDB/Mongo connection string only from environment (e.g., process.env.DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit credentials to the repository or log them; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

practices.practice: Require TLS in client connections (use scheme mongodb+srv with tls=true), use SCRAM-SHA-256 auth and percent-encode credentials when building the URI rather than disabling certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for the client connection (set tls=true / ssl=true and verify the server certificate) when connecting to the managed cluster; do not disable certificate validation in production.

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient / Mongoose connection per process (module-level singleton); do not create a new client per request, and cache the client for serverless warm invocations.
practices.prior_belief: Create and reuse a single Mongoose connection per process (share the mongoose connection across modules), close it gracefully on SIGINT/SIGTERM, and avoid creating a new connection per request.

practices.practice: Set sensible client pool and timeout parameters for your workload (e.g., maxPoolSize, minPoolSize, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and tune them by deployment scenario (small pools for serverless, larger pools for OLTP servers).
practices.prior_belief: Set appropriate Mongo client timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and a reasonable connection pool size (maxPoolSize) to avoid hanging operations and to support expected concurrency.

practices.practice: Be deliberate about driver retry settings (for example, consider retryWrites=false in examples) and ensure application-level retries coexist safely with driver-managed retryable writes (use idempotency or deduplication where needed).

practices.how_found: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Use client sessions and transactions (startSession/withTransaction or startTransaction/commitTransaction), keep transactions short and focused (DocumentDB documents a maximum transaction lifetime of 30 seconds), and commit quickly to limit locks and work done in the transaction.
practices.prior_belief: When running multi-document transactions, keep transactions short and limited to the minimum read/write set (fetch, check, update), avoid long-lived user input inside transactions, and commit as soon as possible to limit locks and RU costs.

practices.practice: Handle transient faults by configuring driver retries and implementing application retries with exponential backoff and limits; design idempotent operations where possible so retries are safe.
practices.prior_belief: When performing transactions, implement a retry loop with exponential backoff and jitter that retries on transient transaction errors (e.g., MongoDB driver labels TransientTransactionError or UnknownTransactionCommitResult) and re-reads necessary documents before retrying.

practices.practice: When decrementing inventory inside a transaction, read the inventory document in-session, assert available >= requested, then perform a conditional update (e.g., updateOne with stock: {$gte: qty} and $inc:-qty) and surface a clear OutOfStock error rather than performing blind decrements.
practices.prior_belief: When decrementing inventory, check available quantity inside the same transaction (e.g., find the inventory doc, assert available >= qty, then update $inc:-qty) and throw a clear OutOfStock error if insufficient, rather than attempting blind decrements.

practices.practice: Create indexes that match your query patterns (single-field, compound, multikey, wildcard, TTL, hashed, 2dsphere as needed); for example create a unique index on inventory.sku and an index on cart.userId to avoid collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes that match your query patterns: at minimum create a unique index on inventory.sku and an index on cart.userId (and a compound index for frequent cart queries like {userId:1, 'items.sku':1}) to avoid COLLSCANs.

practices.practice: Use explain() and read its executionStats to verify that queries use an index (IXSCAN) and do not perform COLLSCANs; iterate index shapes until explain shows index usage for critical queries.

practices.practice: When using DocumentDB vector search, create an explicit vector index and choose the algorithm (DiskANN, HNSW, or IVF) appropriate for your dataset size and latency/recall tradeoff (DiskANN for very large datasets, HNSW for real-time with high recall, IVF for smaller sets); tune index parameters and test recall/latency on representative data.
practices.prior_belief: When using vector search capabilities, create an explicit vector index (choose algorithm: HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) with correct dimensionality and appropriate indexing parameters, and test recall/latency trade-offs on representative data before production use.

practices.practice: Choose shard/partition keys that align with dominant query patterns and provide high cardinality and even distribution; colocate related collections or documents when you need locality for queries or operations.
practices.prior_belief: Choose partition keys so that documents updated together in a transaction are colocated (same partition) where possible — for example, colocate a user's cart and that user's reservation of inventory — to avoid cross-partition transaction limits and high RU/cost.

practices.practice: Use database-side unique constraints (unique indexes) to enforce data integrity, but build unique indexes carefully because unique index builds can block writes on large collections.
practices.prior_belief: Use database-side unique constraints/indexes (unique index on inventory.sku) to ensure data integrity rather than relying only on application checks.

practices.practice: Inspect common server error codes and surface clear domain errors and retryable conditions (for example detect DuplicateKey / E11000, WriteConflict and retry it, and return a typed OutOfStock error for business logic failures).
practices.prior_belief: Detect and surface specific failure modes: return a typed OutOfStock error for insufficient inventory, a Conflict/VersionMismatch error for optimistic concurrency failures, and a TransientError for retryable transaction problems so callers can react appropriately.

practices.practice: For workflows that would require long-lived or large multi-document transactions, prefer reservation/hold patterns (reserve stock, commit later) or break work into smaller steps and release holds on failure/timeouts to avoid long transactions.

notes:
I inspected the sample app files and used Microsoft Learn documentation plus installed DocumentDB skills to discover public best-practice guidance relevant to the app. Many prior beliefs derived from MongoDB / CosmosDB general knowledge are confirmed by Azure DocumentDB docs (connection handling, TLS, single-client reuse, pool/timeouts, transaction lifetime and short transactions, retry/backoff, sharding guidance, indexing, vector index algorithms, monitoring via Azure Monitor, and using explain()). The major contradiction: Azure DocumentDB does not use RU/s pricing — it bills by compute tier and storage rather than request units; guidance that mentions RU/s applies to Cosmos DB (RU-based) not to Azure DocumentDB. Several prior beliefs about Mongoose optimisticConcurrency, explicit readConcern/writeConcern usage, and explicit projection-to-reduce-RU wording had no authoritative DocumentDB page that directly matched them; those remain as prior_knowledge_only and I recorded the searches I ran.

Prior beliefs the discovery step did not classify: K05, K09, K11, K14, K16, K17. See 05a-prior-beliefs.json.
